newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Faulding results depend on approvals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Faulding results depend on approvals.

text.p: Drug manufacturer F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Monday its results for the year to June 30, 1997 were highly dependent on successful commercialism of recently approved products in the United States.

Faulding chief executive ed Tweddell said Faulding had received eight approvals in the U.S. during the six months to December 31 and expected further approvals for both injectable and oral products before June 30 1997.

"However full year 1996/97 profit results are highly dependent on our ability to successfully commercialise these recently approved products," he said in a statement accompanying the half year results.
"In addition, the timing of new approvals and the number of competitive approvals for the same products will impact earnings potential, he said.
Faulding reported a higher net profit of A$16.21 million for the six months to December 1996 compared with A$12.4 million in the previous corresponding half year.
The company said the result reflected a strong performance in the Australian businesses in difficult and highly competitive conditions and a significant improvement in its U.S. operations.

Tweddell said the Chinese market continued to be difficult and Faulding's overall Chinese business would not be profitable for the full year, but the company believed it had the potential to be an important contributor to profits in future.
The company had decided to restructure the operation and to make an abnormal provision of A$7.5 million, a large proportion of which provided for non-payment by distributors, it said.

Tweddell said Faulding expected to have slower sales of its anti-cancer drug Kadian/Kapanol in the second half in the U.S., "but on a full year basis our total Kadian/Kapoanol contribution is expected to be in line with plan".
He said restructuring of Faulding Inc had led to improvements in profitability, driven by an increase in new product approvals and the company expected the trend to continue.
Faulding shares were 25 cents lower at A$7.25 at 2.40 p.m. (0340 GMT).
